name: Marygrove School / Marygrove Services
historical_names: House of the Good Shepherd (St. Louis)
district_operator: Catholic Charities of St. Louis (founded by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd)
notes: The Florissant campus at 2705 Mullanphy Lane was established in 1969 when the Sisters of the Good Shepherd relocated from their Gravois Avenue convent (operated there 1895-1969; the order has served St. Louis since 1849 and counts the institution's heritage to that date). Operated by Catholic Charities of St. Louis since ~1983 (GuideStar EIN 43-1024440, 'Child Center - Marygrove'). The on-campus 'Marygrove School' is a private special-education day school for residents; NCES PSS lists 'Marygrove Services, Inc.' (grades 5-11, nonsectarian) through 2021-22. Organization is still operating (active site, 2024-25 reports), though GuideStar notes residential program consolidation after 2021 - whether the on-campus school still operates as a separate school should be confirmed; the residential program has shrunk. Recommended human follow-up: Catholic Charities program office can confirm current on-campus school status. Note the school serves girls/boys in residential treatment - yearbook output likely minimal or nonexistent.

name: Oak Bridge School
notes: Small private accredited school (MNSAA) at 3465 Shackelford Rd, Florissant, nursery/6 weeks through grade 6, using a Howard Gardner Multiple Intelligences curriculum. Founding date not found online; earliest hard evidence is its first NCES Private School Universe Survey response for 2017-18 (enrollment 40, dropping to 17 by 2021-22) per ProPublica's private-school demographics tool, and the school's own site copyrighted 2018 - so it was operating by ~2017. Currently open and offering tours (oakbridgeschool.org; listed open on third-party directories).

name: Hazelwood High School - Original (Dunn Road)
notes: The first Hazelwood High School building, completed 1954 at 1865 Dunn Road in the Spanish Lake area of unincorporated north St. Louis County, per Hazelwood Central HS's own About Us history page (ninth grade initiated in the district in 1954-55 per the stipulated history in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F. Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975)). Seed's closed year of 1965 is off by one: the second Hazelwood High School was built in 1965 and opened in 1966, ending this building's tenure as the district high school - 1966 is the correct 'closed as Hazelwood HS' year. The building was never demolished or idled: it remained a district school and today houses the Hazelwood Opportunity Center (alternative HS program) at the same address (cross-reference: ALL-476 in another batch). SEED ZIP FLAG: 1865 Dunn Road is ZIP 63138 (Spanish Lake), not 63031. This school is also duplicated as ALL-063/ALL-084/ALL-125/ALL-259/ALL-458/ALL-459 elsewhere in the seed data.

name: Hazelwood High School - Second Building (New Halls Ferry)
notes: The second Hazelwood High School opened in 1966 at 15875 New Halls Ferry Road with 2,515 students in grades 10-12, per the school's own history page (Wikipedia gives 'built 1965, opened 1966'). It never actually closed: 'Hazelwood High School' here is the same institution as today's Hazelwood Central High School (ALL-022) - the 'Central' designator appeared in 1974 to distinguish it from the new East and West schools (opened 1977), so 1974 is recorded as the year this name/identity ended. Row kept separate from ALL-022 per no-silent-merge rule, but this is a rename, not a replacement. The school was so overcrowded it ran split double shifts in 1970-72.

name: Hazelwood Central High School
notes: Continuation of ALL-021 under the 'Central' name adopted ~1974 when Hazelwood East and West opened (they began classes 1977). Some sources, including Wikipedia's infobox, list 'Established 1954' - that counts the whole Hazelwood High School lineage back to the Dunn Road building (ALL-020), not this campus. Still operating at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd (NCES ID 291383000622, ~1,718 students 2024-25). Yearbook name: 'Torch'. Duplicated in other batches as ALL-062/ALL-086/ALL-124/ALL-258/ALL-531 (and mislabeled ALL-460 'Dunn Road Campus').

name: Brown School
district_operator: Brown rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1950)
notes: One-room rural school on the north side of Old Jamestown Road east of Douglas Rd (near Carrico Rd), per Ch. 1 of Franzwa's 1977 'History of the Hazelwood School District' as excerpted by the Old Jamestown Association. Founded when 'Uncle Billy' James deeded 3/4 acre to the school board on December 9, 1859; the brick school was originally called James School, then Douglas and James, finally Brown School (named for the adjoining Brown family - David, Clement, William). Taken over by the new Hazelwood School District in 1950, after which the building became a residence/parsonage for Salem Baptist Church across the street (still standing). Seed's '1950s?' close is consistent. The modern namesake successor serving the area is Brown Elementary (3325 Chickory Creek Lane, brn.hazelwoodschools.org - matches seed 'Current Address'); it appears in other seed batches as ALL-092/ALL-120. Not merged per no-silent-merge rule.

name: Cold Water School
district_operator: Cold Water rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1950)
notes: County District #2. A log Cold Water School near Vaile & Old Halls Ferry Rd existed by the 1840s (the school the Brown School pupils were walking miles to, per Franzwa ch. 1); it burned in 1850 and the surviving one-room brick building was built in 1859 (150th anniversary celebrated 2009, per the Hazelwood district press release carried by flovalleynews.com). Annexed into Hazelwood School District February 18, 1950; closed spring 1954 per the St. Louis County landmarks page. Building survives as a museum on the HSD Learning Center grounds at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd, in front of Hazelwood Central HS. Namesake modern successor: Cold Water Elementary, 1105 Wiethaupt Rd (cws.hazelwoodschools.org - matches seed 'Current Address'); appears in other batches as ALL-093/ALL-119. Building-dating nuance: opened_year left unknown because the school entity predates 1859 (the 1859 date is the surviving building).

name: Prigge School / Larimore School
district_operator: Prigge (Larimore) rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1951)
notes: CONFLATED NAME: 'Prigge' and 'Larimore' are not two schools - per Franzwa's 1977 district history (Ch. 6), 'Prigge is the predecessor name for the Larimore district.' The Prigge district elected to join Hazelwood in a special election on July 29, 1951. Franzwa notes at least three 'Prigge'-annotated schoolhouse sites on a 1927 map (named for Charles F. Prigge family), plus a possible 'colored school' on Prigge land whose location is unrecorded. The school line continued as Larimore; the namesake modern successor is Larimore Elementary, 1025 Trampe Lane (63138, lar.hazelwoodschools.org), appearing in other batches as ALL-464/ALL-534. Closed_year 1951 = end of independent-district operation, not necessarily last day classes met in the building.

name: Hyatt School
district_operator: Hyatt rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: County District #10 per a sibling seed row (ALL-254, 'Closed/Converted'). One of the 13 schoolhouses that became the Hazelwood School District (district press release via flovalleynews.com, 2009). Located on/near Shackelford Road; almost certainly named for the Hyatt family whose farms anchored that area - the Joseph Hyatt House (2625 Shackelford Rd, c.1860) is a St. Louis County landmark. Exact annexation/closure year not found; '1951' recorded as probable = end of the district's 1949-1951 annexation window documented in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F. Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975). Building may have continued as a Hazelwood district school afterward. No namesake modern school.

name: Elm Grove School
district_operator: Elm Grove rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: County District #9; established 1852, one of the earliest school buildings in the county. Closed 1952 'following the organization of the Hazelwood School District' per the City of Hazelwood historical marker; building moved to Brookes Park (450 Brookes Dr, Hazelwood 63042) in 1966 (Esley Hamilton's St. Louis County rural-schools survey says rebuilt in the park 1961 - minor discrepancy) and is preserved as 'The Little Red Schoolhouse,' a county landmark. SEED FLAG: address '450 Brookes Lane' is the relocated-museum site at 450 Brookes Dr, Hazelwood (ZIP 63042, not 63031), not the original school location, which I could not pin down online. A sibling seed row 'Old Elm Grove School' (ALL-249, ZIP 63045, 'Closed/Relocated') is the same school/building.

name: Pea Ridge School
district_operator: Pea Ridge rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Verified as a real school: USGS GNIS 'Pea Ridge School' (N38.810882, W90.195388) appears on the Columbia Bottom, MO topo quad in north St. Louis County (topoquest.com listing). One of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into the Hazelwood School District 1949-1951 (federal court stipulation, 392 F. Supp. 1276; district press release list via flovalleynews.com). 1951 = end of the documented annexation window; exact school-level closure year not found online. Building no longer stands or is a private residence. No successor school identified - students would have fed Hazelwood district elementaries.

name: Columbia Bottom School
district_operator: Columbia Bottom rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Named in the Hazelwood district's own 2009 list of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into the district (via flovalleynews.com) and in the 1949-1951 annexation history stipulated in 392 F. Supp. 1276. Presumably in the Columbia Bottoms/Columbia Bottom Road area at the confluence of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers (northeast corner of the county - the 'Columbia Bottom' USGS quad); no building record or dates found online. 1951 = probable end of independent operation. Nothing further found; likely requires Franzwa's 1977 'History of the Hazelwood School District' (print) or county deed records - recommended human follow-up.

name: Vossenkemper School
district_operator: Vossenkemper rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Verified real: one of the 13 Hazelwood-consolidation schoolhouses (district press release list, flovalleynews.com 2009). Located at Robbins Mill (later Highway 67) near Jamestown per the 1989 St. Louis County North historic buildings inventory (Esley Hamilton, Phase II: Black Jack); also annotated as a family-named school on the 1935 USGS Columbia Bottom topo sheet (pastmaps.com). No operating dates found; '1951' = probable end of independent operation in the 1949-1951 annexation window. Likely named for the Vossenkemper family of the New Bielefeld/Black Jack area.

name: Black Jack School
district_operator: Black Jack rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: One of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into Hazelwood School District (1949-1951 window; court stipulation + district press release list). The community's school lot at what is now Black Jack City Hall (4655 Parker Road) was purchased by the local school board in the 1850s; the surviving 1928 school building at that address is now Black Jack City Hall per the St. Louis County historic buildings inventory. Not to be confused with the Salem Lutheran/Parker Road School (1895, private Lutheran school, county landmark) on the same road. ZIP: Black Jack addresses are 63033, not seed's 63031. No post-consolidation dates found; whether the 1928 building operated as a Hazelwood district school past 1951 is unresolved.

name: McCluer North High School
notes: Seed's 1971 opening confirmed: founded 1971 at 705 Waterford Drive (bounded by St. Catherine and Parker Rd, facing the Florissant Civic Center) to relieve the original McCluer High School (built for 3,300, enrollment 4,500+ by 1971 with split sessions); students split into McCluer North and McCluer High Schools beginning with the 1972-73 year per the McCluer HS history. Still operating (mnhs.fergflor.org; 'Stars'). Sister schools elsewhere in the seed: McCluer HS (ALL-111 etc.) and McCluer South-Berkeley HS (ALL-113 etc.).
